question: An analyst must deliver a carefully reasoned briefing by the end of the day and has limited allowance left. Which sequence of steps is correct?
options: A) Check it against the brief; cut the scope to what the briefing needs; run that scope on the deepest tier; expand it if time allows.
B) Cut the scope to what the briefing actually needs; run that scope on the deepest tier; check it against the brief; expand it if time allows.
C) Run the full scope on the deepest tier; cut the scope to what the briefing needs; check it against the brief; expand it if time allows.
D) Cut the scope to what the briefing actually needs; expand it if time allows; run that scope on the deepest tier; check it against the brief.
correct_answers: B) Cut the scope to what the briefing actually needs; run that scope on the deepest tier; check it against the brief; expand it if time allows.
explanations: Incorrect. Checking comes before anything has been produced, which makes the first step impossible.
Correct. Narrowing scope is what makes the deeper tier affordable within the remaining allowance, and the check confirms the reduced briefing still meets the requirement.
Incorrect. Running the full scope on the most expensive tier first spends the constrained allowance before any trimming happens.
Incorrect. Expanding the scope before it has been produced undoes the trimming that made the deeper tier affordable.
